chunks.arabic_text: وَلَهُ رِوَايَةٌ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: He has a narration from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). Weak.

en.summary: Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sarrāj, a Kufan narrator from the generation following the Imams, is recorded in al-Ghadāʾirī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* as having transmitted traditions from Imām al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him). His classification as 'weak' (ḍaʿīf) highlights the rigorous scrutiny applied to the chain of transmission (isnād) in Shia hadith sciences, ensuring that even those close to the Imams were evaluated for reliability before their narrations were accepted as authoritative.
en.seo_question: Who is Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sarrāj and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ السَّرَّاجِ: Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sarrāj, the narrator's name
key_terms.كَوْفِيٌّ: Kufan, indicating origin from the city of Kufa
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, honorific for Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term for a narrator whose reliability is not established
